maya: heads-up — after NCCL bump to 2.18 on the prod inference pool (region: us-west-2, nodepool: inf-gpu-a100-8) we're seeing intermittent hangs/timeouts on 8x A100 jobs. started ~08:10 UTC after the maintenance window. can we triage? :exclamation:

sam: oof. any errors in the logs? which workloads affected (batch size / seq len)?

maya: mostly multi-GPU beam-gen and chat-infer jobs with kv-cache. seq lens ~512, batch 16 across 8 gpus. errors: workers stuck in collective ops, job doesn't progress for minutes then OOM on host side. pod restarts clear it.

alex: paste from one of the stuck pods' nccl debug: ```
NCCL INFO NET/IB : Using ibverbs; peer: 10.12.45.9
NCCL WARN NET : Timeout waiting for allreduce progress
NCCL INFO COLL : allgather start
... waiting (120s) ...
NCCL ERROR TIMEOUT coll allgather
```
Looks like collectives stall, then timeout. no obvious driver crash.

kai: two quick hypotheses: 1) NCCL 2.18 changed fallback behavior w/ SHM vs IB and we might be hitting an RDMA incompat (firmware or mlx drivers) 2) a kernel driver/CUDA mismatch causing hangs under heavy IPC. Can you confirm kernel/driver versions on affected nodes?

maya: node info from one host: ```
Linux 5.15.0-112-generic
NVIDIA Driver 535.54
CUDA runtime 12.2
NCCL 2.18.1-rc
MLX FW 14.26.1010
```
We did the NCCL bump in the image only — GPUs had same driver.

sam: try running quick repro with env vars to force path changes: set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 and NCCL_SHM_DISABLE=0 and see if it shifts behavior. also try NCCL_DEBUG=INFO to get richer traces.

maya: running those now on a canary job. command: ```
export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1
python run_infer.py --model gpt-xx --gpus 8 --batch 16 --seq 512
```

deploy-bot: canary job 1760918412 deployed to pool inf-gpu-a100-8-canary (image: inference:2026-03-18-nccl2.18) :white_check_mark:

alex: FYI I repro'd locally on a 4x A100 dev box — with NCCL 2.18 collectives slow and threads stuck in ncclAllReduce for >60s. Downgrading to 2.16 removed the stall.

kai: that narrows it. sounds like a regression in 2.18's transport selection. workarounds: force tcp or shm (NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME, NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL maybe), or pin NCCL to 2.16 for now. also check IB firmware + mlx driver versions; some mlx updates included a bugfix that older nccl versions tolerated differently.

maya: can we do an emergency rollback for the pool? I'd prefer minimal blast radius — rollback the image in the controlled canary then batch rollback across regions if no issues.

sam: agree. schedule: 1) rollback pool-canary to nccl 2.16 image (now), 2) run 2 hours of smoke and perf checks, 3) if green, rollback inf-gpu-a100-8 pool (staggered). I'll open a rollback RFC and mark high priority.

maya: smoke results after NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 on canary: no hangs in 30m, throughput ~-6% but stable. leaving tests running.

alex: log snippet when disabling IB: ```
NCCL INFO NET/TCP : Using 10.12.x.x
allgather complete in 120ms
```
So path change avoids stall.

kai: please also capture /var/log/messages and dmesg around the hangs; if there are mlx driver WARNs or kernel oops patterns we need to file with NVIDIA/Mellanox.

maya: copying logs to /shared/snapshots/1760918400-nccl-hang/ (I'll drop a link once uploaded).

deploy-bot: alert created: INC-2026-03-18-004 (nccl 2.18 hangs) assigned to eng-runtime, sev:high

sam: action items: - rollback image on canary now (maya) - run targeted perf tests w/ NCCL 2.16 vs 2.18 (alex) - collect host mlx/fw + kernel + driver matrix across affected nodes (kai) - open vendor ticket with NVIDIA/Mellanox and attach nccl traces (maya)

maya: rolling canary back now. will post follow-ups. thanks all. :pray:
